conditions.title: Scapula anterior tilt
conditions.tags: Shoulder impingement, upper crossed syndrome
conditions.tightMuscles: Pectoralis minor, latissimus dorsi, coracobrachialis
conditions.weakMuscles: Lower trapezius, serratus anterior
conditions.screening: Overhead squat: arms fall forward
conditions.summary: Anterior tipping of the scapula can reduce comfortable overhead mechanics and contribute to shoulder compensation.

conditions.title: Round shoulder
conditions.tags: Upper crossed syndrome, shoulder impingement, rib flare
conditions.tightMuscles: Pectoralis minor, pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi
conditions.weakMuscles: Rhomboids, lower trapezius, middle trapezius
conditions.screening: Standing posture and overhead squat
conditions.summary: A forward shoulder position commonly combines restricted anterior tissue with reduced scapular control.

conditions.title: Anterior pelvic tilt
conditions.tags: Pelvic position, hip extension, trunk control
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; hip flexors and lumbar extensors may contribute
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; abdominal and hip-extensor control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe standing pelvic position, then compare it with a controlled pelvic tilt and hip-extension task
conditions.summary: An anterior pelvic tilt is a position or movement strategy, not a diagnosis. The useful question is whether the person can comfortably move out of it and control the pelvis during relevant tasks.

conditions.title: Posterior pelvic tilt
conditions.tags: Pelvic position, lumbar flexion, hip mechanics
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; posterior hip or abdominal tension may contribute
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; lumbar extensor and hip-flexor control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Compare relaxed standing with controlled anterior and posterior pelvic tilting and a hip-hinge task
conditions.summary: A posterior pelvic tilt describes pelvic position, not damage. Assessment should focus on available motion, comfort, and control during the tasks that matter.

conditions.title: Forward head posture
conditions.tags: Head position, neck comfort, thoracic position
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; suboccipital and superficial cervical muscles may contribute
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; deep cervical flexor endurance and thoracic control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe the head over the rib cage, then assess comfortable cervical retraction, rotation, and thoracic extension
conditions.summary: Forward head posture is common and does not by itself prove injury. What matters is whether neck position is comfortable, adaptable, and controlled during daily activity.

conditions.title: Rib flare
conditions.joints: Rib cage, thoracic spine, lumbar spine
conditions.tags: Breathing, trunk position, overhead movement
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; lumbar extensors and accessory breathing muscles may contribute
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; abdominal wall coordination and expiratory control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe breathing and rib movement at rest, then during reaching, arm elevation, and a controlled exhale
conditions.summary: Rib flare describes a visible rib-cage position. It is best explored through breathing, trunk control, and task-specific movement rather than treated as a fixed deformity.

conditions.title: Knee valgus pattern
conditions.tags: Knee alignment, squat, landing, gait
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; assess hip, ankle, and foot mobility rather than assuming one tight muscle
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; hip, knee, and foot control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe knee direction during a squat, step-down, walking, or landing and compare with foot and hip motion
conditions.summary: A valgus movement pattern means the knee moves inward relative to the hip and foot during a task. Its relevance depends on control, symptoms, load, and the specific activity.

conditions.title: Knee varus pattern
conditions.tags: Knee alignment, squat, gait, lateral loading
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; assess hip, ankle, and foot mobility rather than assuming one tight muscle
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; hip, knee, and foot control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe knee direction during a squat, step-down, and walking while noting pressure through the foot
conditions.summary: A varus movement pattern means the knee remains or moves outward relative to the hip and foot. It should be interpreted in the context of symptoms, task, and individual anatomy.

conditions.title: Foot valgus / pronation pattern
conditions.tags: Pronation, arch control, gait, balance
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; calf or lateral lower-leg mobility may be relevant
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; intrinsic-foot and lower-leg control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe the rearfoot, arch, and pressure distribution during standing, heel raises, and walking
conditions.summary: A valgus or pronation pattern describes how the foot adapts toward the ground. Some pronation is normal; the useful question is whether it is comfortable, controlled, and appropriate for the task.

conditions.title: Foot varus / supination pattern
conditions.tags: Supination, lateral foot pressure, gait, balance
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; plantar-flexor or medial lower-leg mobility may be relevant
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; peroneal and intrinsic-foot control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Observe the rearfoot, arch, and pressure distribution during standing, heel raises, and walking
conditions.summary: A varus or supination pattern describes a tendency to load the outer foot or maintain a higher arch. Its importance depends on comfort, adaptability, and task demands.

conditions.title: Early heel rise
conditions.tags: Squat, gait, ankle dorsiflexion, calf control
conditions.tightMuscles: Calf or ankle restriction may contribute, but the pattern can also reflect balance or strategy
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; foot, calf, and proximal control may be relevant
conditions.screening: Note when the heel lifts during a squat or walking, then compare ankle range, balance, and stance width
conditions.summary: An early heel rise can reflect ankle range, balance, body proportions, or movement strategy. It should be assessed in the task where it appears.

conditions.title: Asymmetric hip shift
conditions.tags: Squat, stance, side-to-side loading, pelvic control
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; compare hip and ankle mobility on both sides
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; compare lateral hip, trunk, and leg control on both sides
conditions.screening: Observe side-to-side loading during stance, squat, step-down, and single-leg balance
conditions.summary: An asymmetric hip shift describes unequal side-to-side loading. It may reflect mobility, strength, comfort, habit, or task setup and should not be reduced to one muscle.

conditions.title: Elevated shoulder
conditions.tags: Shoulder height, scapular position, neck tension
conditions.tightMuscles: Pattern-dependent; upper trapezius, levator scapulae, or protective tension may contribute
conditions.weakMuscles: Pattern-dependent; scapular control and trunk support may be relevant
conditions.screening: Compare resting shoulder height with reaching, arm elevation, breathing, and comfortable neck movement
conditions.summary: An elevated shoulder may be a temporary strategy, a side-to-side habit, or a response to discomfort. Focus on adaptable movement rather than forcing symmetry.

conditions.title: Ankle sprain recovery
conditions.tags: Balance, mobility, stability, return to movement
conditions.tightMuscles: Varies by injury stage and individual presentation
conditions.weakMuscles: Calf and lateral ankle strength may require progressive rebuilding
conditions.screening: Comfortable walking, swelling response, ankle range, balance, and task tolerance
conditions.summary: An ankle sprain involves ligament injury of varying severity. Recovery should match the injury stage and rebuild comfortable motion, balance, strength, and task tolerance.

conditions.title: Knee sprain recovery
conditions.tags: Ligament sprain, swelling, instability, return to activity
conditions.tightMuscles: Muscle guarding and motion loss vary with the injured structure and stage
conditions.weakMuscles: Quadriceps, hamstrings, calf, and hip capacity may need graded rebuilding after assessment
conditions.screening: A traumatic twist, marked swelling, inability to bear weight, locking, giving way, or persistent instability warrants clinical assessment before exercise progression.
conditions.summary: A knee sprain is a ligament injury that can range from mild fibre damage to a complete tear. The mechanism, swelling, stability, and ability to bear weight help determine whether self-guided exercise is appropriate.
conditions.sourceName: AAOS OrthoInfo — Sprains, Strains & Other Soft-Tissue Injuries

conditions.title: Wrist sprain recovery
conditions.tags: Ligament sprain, fall on an outstretched hand, grip, loading
conditions.tightMuscles: Protective forearm tension and wrist stiffness may occur after injury
conditions.weakMuscles: Grip and wrist capacity may need gradual rebuilding once a fracture or major ligament injury is excluded
conditions.screening: Pain after a fall, focal bony tenderness, deformity, marked swelling, numbness, or pain that does not improve requires assessment before loading the wrist.
conditions.summary: A wrist sprain can follow a fall or forceful twist, but fractures and more significant ligament injuries can look similar. Confirm the diagnosis before progressing weight-bearing or grip work.
conditions.sourceName: AAOS OrthoInfo — Sprains, Strains & Other Soft-Tissue Injuries

conditions.title: Shoulder dislocation recovery
conditions.tags: Dislocation, instability, apprehension, return to overhead activity
conditions.tightMuscles: Protective guarding may temporarily limit shoulder motion
conditions.weakMuscles: Rotator-cuff, scapular, and arm capacity may require a staged return after medical management
conditions.screening: A suspected dislocation needs urgent medical care and should not be self-reduced. New numbness, weakness, vascular changes, repeat instability, or severe pain requires assessment.
conditions.summary: A shoulder dislocation is a joint injury, not simply a movement fault. Exercise belongs after the joint has been reduced and the person has received appropriate assessment and stage-specific guidance.

conditions.title: Cervical radicular symptoms
conditions.tags: Radiating arm pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, nerve-root irritation
conditions.tightMuscles: Muscle tension may accompany symptoms but does not identify the affected nerve or cause
conditions.weakMuscles: Objective arm or hand weakness needs clinical assessment rather than generic strengthening
conditions.screening: Progressive weakness, loss of hand function, altered walking, symptoms in both arms, severe trauma, or bowel or bladder changes requires prompt medical evaluation.
conditions.summary: Cervical radicular symptoms can include neck-to-arm pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness when a cervical nerve root is irritated or compressed. Similar symptoms can come from other sites, so diagnosis matters.

conditions.title: Sciatica and radiating leg symptoms
conditions.tags: Sciatica, leg pain, tingling, numbness, nerve irritation
conditions.tightMuscles: Muscle tension may coexist but does not explain all radiating leg symptoms
conditions.weakMuscles: New or progressive leg weakness requires assessment before exercise selection
conditions.screening: Numbness around the saddle area, loss of bladder or bowel control, rapidly worsening weakness, symptoms in both legs, fever, or major trauma requires urgent medical care.
conditions.summary: Sciatica describes symptoms along the sciatic-nerve pathway and may involve leg pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness. It is different from isolated low-back pain and should be screened for neurological change.

conditions.title: Lumbar disc-related symptoms
conditions.tags: Disc herniation, back pain, leg symptoms, load tolerance
conditions.tightMuscles: Protective trunk and hip tension can occur but is not a diagnosis
conditions.weakMuscles: Capacity changes should be assessed in context; neurological weakness needs clinical review
conditions.screening: New bladder or bowel change, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, unexplained weight loss, cancer history, or major trauma requires urgent or prompt assessment.
conditions.summary: Disc changes are common and do not automatically explain pain. When disc material irritates a nerve root, symptoms may include radiating leg pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness and need an appropriate clinical screen.

conditions.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.tags: Median nerve, numbness, tingling, night symptoms, grip
conditions.tightMuscles: Local tissue tension may coexist, but carpal tunnel syndrome involves pressure on the median nerve at the wrist
conditions.weakMuscles: Persistent thumb weakness or difficulty handling small objects warrants clinical assessment
conditions.screening: Persistent numbness, worsening weakness, muscle loss at the thumb, symptoms after trauma, or unclear symptom distribution should be professionally assessed.
conditions.summary: Carpal tunnel syndrome occurs when the median nerve is compressed at the wrist. Symptoms commonly involve numbness or tingling in the thumb, index, middle, and part of the ring finger and may be worse at night.

muscles.title: Serratus anterior
muscles.origin: Upper eight or nine ribs
muscles.insertion: Anterior medial border of the scapula
muscles.actions: Protracts the scapula, assists upward rotation, and helps hold the scapula against the rib cage.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration highlighting the serratus anterior muscle on the side of the rib cage
muscles.imageCredit: Serratus anterior, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Lower trapezius
muscles.origin: Lower thoracic spinous processes
muscles.insertion: Medial end of the scapular spine
muscles.actions: The lower fibers assist scapular depression and upward rotation and contribute to posterior tilt during arm elevation.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Anatomography animation color-coding the lower trapezius fibers
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Pectoralis minor
muscles.origin: Ribs three to five
muscles.insertion: Coracoid process of the scapula
muscles.actions: Draws the scapula anteriorly and inferiorly against the thoracic wall, contributing to scapular downward rotation, and may assist forced inspiration when the scapula is fixed.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the pectoralis minor muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Pixelsquid, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Manubrium of the sternum and medial clavicle
muscles.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone and lateral superior nuchal line
muscles.actions: Bilaterally flexes the neck; unilaterally laterally flexes to the same side and rotates the head to the opposite side.
muscles.imageAlt: Lateral anatomical illustration highlighting the sternocleidomastoid muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Levator scapulae
muscles.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the upper four cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the scapula above the scapular spine
muscles.actions: Elevates and downwardly rotates the scapula; with the scapula fixed, assists neck extension and same-side lateral flexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the levator scapulae muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Splenius capitis
muscles.origin: Lower nuchal ligament and spinous processes of the lower cervical and upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line
muscles.actions: Bilaterally extends the head and neck; unilaterally rotates and laterally flexes the head to the same side.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the splenius capitis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Semispinalis capitis
muscles.origin: Transverse and articular processes of the upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Occipital bone between the nuchal lines
muscles.actions: Extends the head and neck and rotates the head to the opposite side.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior three-dimensional anatomical view distinctly highlighting the semispinalis capitis in red
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Deltoid
muscles.origin: Lateral clavicle, acromion, and spine of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
muscles.actions: Primarily abducts the arm; anterior fibers assist flexion and medial rotation, while posterior fibers assist extension and lateral rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration highlighting the deltoid muscle around the shoulder
muscles.imageCredit: Chrizz, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Pectoralis major
muscles.origin: Medial clavicle, sternum, and costal cartilages of the upper ribs
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
muscles.actions: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; the clavicular fibers assist shoulder flexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the pectoralis major muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, colorized by Michael Gasperl, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.origin: Lower thoracic vertebrae, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, and lower ribs
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
muscles.actions: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration of the latissimus dorsi muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Leo Testut, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Biceps brachii
muscles.origin: Coracoid process and supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Radial tuberosity and forearm fascia through the bicipital aponeurosis
muscles.actions: Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; also assists shoulder flexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration highlighting the biceps brachii on the front of the upper arm
muscles.imageCredit: Chrizz, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Triceps brachii
muscles.origin: Infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and posterior humerus
muscles.insertion: Olecranon of the ulna
muscles.actions: Extends the elbow; the long head also assists shoulder extension and adduction.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration of the triceps brachii muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Leo Testut, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Lateral distal radius near the styloid process
muscles.actions: Flexes the elbow most effectively with the forearm in a neutral position.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration highlighting the brachioradialis muscle in the forearm
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, adapted by Selket, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Supraspinatus
muscles.origin: Supraspinous fossa of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
muscles.actions: Initiates arm abduction and helps stabilize the humeral head in the shoulder socket.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior 3D anatomy view with the supraspinatus muscle highlighted in red
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Infraspinatus
muscles.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the arm and helps stabilize the humeral head in the shoulder socket.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior 3D anatomy view with the infraspinatus muscle highlighted in red
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Teres minor
muscles.origin: Middle lateral border of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the arm, assists adduction, and helps stabilize the shoulder joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Lateral 3D anatomy view with the teres minor muscle highlighted in red
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Subscapularis
muscles.origin: Subscapular fossa of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Lesser tubercle of the humerus
muscles.actions: Medially rotates and adducts the arm and helps stabilize the humeral head.
muscles.imageAlt: Frontal 3D anatomy view with the subscapularis muscle highlighted in red
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Teres major
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
muscles.actions: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical rendering highlighting the teres major muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Rhomboid major
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the scapula from the scapular spine to the inferior angle
muscles.actions: Retracts and downwardly rotates the scapula and helps hold it against the thoracic wall.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the rhomboid major muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Brachialis
muscles.origin: Distal anterior surface of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
muscles.actions: Primary elbow flexor in all forearm positions.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the brachialis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, adapted by Selket, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Pronator teres
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus and coronoid process of the ulna
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the mid-radius
muscles.actions: Pronates the forearm and assists elbow flexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the pronator teres muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor carpi radialis
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Bases of the second and third metacarpals
muscles.actions: Flexes and abducts the wrist.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the flexor carpi radialis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Selket, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor carpi radialis longus
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Base of the second metacarpal
muscles.actions: Extends and abducts the wrist and contributes to wrist stability during gripping.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor carpi radialis longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Rectus abdominis
muscles.origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages of ribs five through seven
muscles.actions: Flexes the trunk, compresses abdominal contents, and assists control of pelvic position.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the rectus abdominis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Chrizz, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: External oblique
muscles.origin: External surfaces of ribs five through twelve
muscles.insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle, and anterior iliac crest
muscles.actions: Compresses the abdomen; flexes and laterally flexes the trunk; rotates the trunk to the opposite side.
muscles.imageAlt: OpenStax layered abdominal wall illustration identifying the external oblique muscle
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Transversus abdominis
muscles.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, inguinal ligament, and internal surfaces of lower costal cartilages
muscles.insertion: Linea alba and pubis
muscles.actions: Compresses and supports abdominal contents and contributes to trunk stabilization and forced expiration.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the transversus abdominis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Diaphragm
muscles.origin: Xiphoid process, lower ribs and costal cartilages, and upper lumbar vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Central tendon of the diaphragm
muscles.actions: Primary muscle of inspiration; contraction increases thoracic volume and supports pressure management through the trunk.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical line illustration of the human diaphragm
muscles.imageCredit: Pearson Scott Foresman, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Internal oblique
muscles.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior iliac crest, and lateral inguinal ligament
muscles.insertion: Lower ribs, linea alba, and pubis
muscles.actions: Compresses the abdomen; flexes and laterally flexes the trunk; rotates the trunk to the same side.
muscles.imageAlt: OpenStax layered abdominal wall illustration identifying the internal oblique muscle
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Multifidus
muscles.origin: Posterior sacrum, posterior superior iliac spine, and transverse processes from lumbar through cervical regions
muscles.insertion: Spinous processes two to four vertebral levels above
muscles.actions: Stabilizes vertebral segments and assists spinal extension and opposite-side rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the multifidus muscles along the spine
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Quadratus lumborum
muscles.origin: Posterior iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament
muscles.insertion: Twelfth rib and transverse processes of the upper lumbar vertebrae
muscles.actions: Laterally flexes and extends the trunk and stabilizes the twelfth rib during breathing.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the quadratus lumborum muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: External intercostals
muscles.origin: Inferior border of each rib
muscles.insertion: Superior border of the rib below
muscles.actions: Elevate the ribs and support expansion of the thoracic cavity during inspiration.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model distinctly highlighting the external intercostals between the ribs
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Gluteus maximus
muscles.origin: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx, and sacrotuberous ligament
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur
muscles.actions: Extends and laterally rotates the hip and contributes to powerful rising, climbing, and propulsion.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomy plate highlighting the gluteus maximus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, adapted by Mikael Häggström, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gluteus medius
muscles.origin: External surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter of the femur
muscles.actions: Abducts the hip and helps stabilize the pelvis during single-leg support; anterior fibers assist medial rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomography 3D anatomical illustration isolating the gluteus medius muscle on the pelvis and femur
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor longus
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis inferior to the pubic crest
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera of the femur
muscles.actions: Adducts the hip and assists hip flexion and medial rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the adductor longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Berichard, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Rectus femoris
muscles.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and ilium superior to the acetabulum
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity through the quadriceps tendon, patella, and patellar ligament
muscles.actions: Extends the knee and flexes the hip.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the rectus femoris muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Biceps femoris
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity and linea aspera of the femur
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula
muscles.actions: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the flexed leg; the long head also extends the hip.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the long head of the biceps femoris muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Mikael Haggstrom, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gluteus minimus
muscles.origin: External surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines
muscles.insertion: Anterior surface of the greater trochanter of the femur
muscles.actions: Abducts and medially rotates the hip and assists pelvic stability during single-leg support.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical rendering highlighting the gluteus minimus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Tensor fasciae latae
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and adjacent anterior iliac crest
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract
muscles.actions: Flexes, abducts, and medially rotates the hip and helps stabilize the knee through the iliotibial tract.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the tensor fasciae latae muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Piriformis
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum
muscles.insertion: Superior border of the greater trochanter of the femur
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the extended hip, abducts the flexed hip, and assists stabilization of the femoral head.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomy plate highlighting the piriformis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, adapted by Mikael Häggström, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor magnus
muscles.origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus, and ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of the femur
muscles.actions: Adducts the hip; the adductor portion assists flexion while the hamstring portion assists extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical rendering highlighting the adductor magnus muscle of the medial thigh
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gracilis
muscles.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
muscles.insertion: Medial proximal tibia through the pes anserinus
muscles.actions: Adducts the hip and flexes and medially rotates the knee.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical rendering highlighting the gracilis muscle of the medial thigh
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Sartorius
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine
muscles.insertion: Medial proximal tibia through the pes anserinus
muscles.actions: Flexes, abducts, and laterally rotates the hip and flexes the knee.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the sartorius muscle across the thigh
muscles.imageCredit: U.S. Government illustration, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Vastus lateralis
muscles.origin: Greater trochanter and lateral lip of the linea aspera of the femur
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity through the quadriceps tendon, patella, and patellar ligament
muscles.actions: Extends the knee and contributes to control of the patella through the quadriceps tendon.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the vastus lateralis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Vastus medialis
muscles.origin: Intertrochanteric line and medial lip of the linea aspera of the femur
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity through the quadriceps tendon, patella, and patellar ligament
muscles.actions: Extends the knee and contributes to medial control of the patella through the quadriceps tendon.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the vastus medialis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Semitendinosus
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: Medial proximal tibia through the pes anserinus
muscles.actions: Extends the hip, flexes the knee, and medially rotates the flexed leg.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical rendering highlighting the semitendinosus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Semimembranosus
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: Posterior medial condyle of the tibia
muscles.actions: Extends the hip, flexes the knee, and medially rotates the flexed leg.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical rendering highlighting the semimembranosus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Tibialis anterior
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle and upper lateral surface of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal
muscles.actions: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot and helps control the foot as it lowers during walking.
muscles.imageAlt: Three-dimensional anatomical rendering highlighting the tibialis anterior muscle
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Gastrocnemius
muscles.origin: Posterior surfaces of the medial and lateral femoral condyles
muscles.insertion: Posterior calcaneus through the calcaneal tendon
muscles.actions: Plantarflexes the ankle and assists knee flexion; contributes strongly to propulsion.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the gastrocnemius muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Chrizz, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Soleus
muscles.origin: Posterior fibular head and proximal fibula, and soleal line of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Posterior calcaneus through the calcaneal tendon
muscles.actions: Plantarflexes the ankle and plays an important postural role during standing and walking.
muscles.imageAlt: Anatomical illustration of the soleus muscle and its tendinous arch
muscles.imageCredit: Johannes Sobotta, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Fibularis longus
muscles.origin: Head and upper lateral surface of the fibula
muscles.insertion: Base of the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform on the plantar foot
muscles.actions: Everts and plantarflexes the foot and helps support the transverse and lateral arches.
muscles.imageAlt: Lateral anatomical illustration highlighting the fibularis longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Fibularis brevis
muscles.origin: Distal lateral surface of the fibula
muscles.insertion: Tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal
muscles.actions: Everts and assists plantarflexion of the foot and contributes to lateral ankle control.
muscles.imageAlt: Lateral anatomical rendering isolating the fibularis brevis in the outer lower-leg compartment
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Tibialis posterior
muscles.origin: Posterior tibia, posterior fibula, and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Navicular tuberosity with expansions to the midfoot tarsals and bases of the middle metatarsals
muscles.actions: Plantarflexes and inverts the foot and supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomy plate highlighting the tibialis posterior muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, adapted by Uwe Gille, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor hallucis longus
muscles.origin: Posterior distal fibula and adjacent interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.actions: Flexes the great toe, assists plantarflexion, and contributes to push-off and arch support.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the flexor hallucis longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor hallucis longus
muscles.origin: Middle anterior fibula and adjacent interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.actions: Extends the great toe and assists ankle dorsiflexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical illustration highlighting the extensor hallucis longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor digitorum longus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of toes two through five
muscles.actions: Flexes the lateral four toes, assists plantarflexion and inversion, and supports the longitudinal arches.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the flexor digitorum longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor digitorum longus
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, anterior fibula, and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes two through five
muscles.actions: Extends the lateral four toes and assists ankle dorsiflexion and foot eversion.
muscles.imageAlt: Anterior anatomical rendering highlighting the extensor digitorum longus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Longissimus capitis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae and articular processes of the lower cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Posterior margin of the mastoid process of the temporal bone
muscles.actions: Extends the head and neck bilaterally and laterally flexes and rotates the head to the same side unilaterally.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy posterior plate highlighting the longissimus column up to longissimus capitis
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Longus colli
muscles.origin: Anterior surfaces of the upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebral bodies and cervical transverse processes
muscles.insertion: Anterior tubercle of the atlas, upper cervical vertebral bodies, and cervical transverse processes
muscles.actions: Flexes and stabilizes the cervical spine and assists slight rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy anterior neck plate highlighting longus colli along the cervical vertebral bodies
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Longus capitis
muscles.origin: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the third through sixth cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Basilar part of the occipital bone
muscles.actions: Flexes the head and upper cervical spine and contributes to anterior cervical control.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy anterior neck plate highlighting longus capitis from the cervical transverse processes to the occiput
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Upper trapezius
muscles.origin: External occipital protuberance, medial superior nuchal line, and ligamentum nuchae
muscles.insertion: Lateral third of the clavicle and acromion
muscles.actions: Elevates the scapula and contributes to upward rotation; with the shoulder girdle fixed it can assist neck extension and side bending.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Anatomography animation color-coding the upper trapezius fibers
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Middle trapezius
muscles.origin: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments of the upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Acromion and superior lip of the scapular spine
muscles.actions: Retracts the scapula and assists scapular control during reaching and pulling.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Anatomography animation color-coding the middle trapezius fibers
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Rhomboid minor
muscles.origin: Ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of the seventh cervical and first thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Medial end of the scapular spine
muscles.actions: Retracts and downwardly rotates the scapula and helps secure it to the thoracic wall.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical illustration highlighting the rhomboid minor
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor carpi ulnaris
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus, olecranon, and posterior border of the ulna
muscles.insertion: Pisiform, hook of hamate, and base of the fifth metacarpal
muscles.actions: Flexes and adducts the hand at the wrist.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused anatomy illustration highlighting the flexor carpi ulnaris in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Palmaris longus
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis
muscles.actions: Flexes the wrist and tensions the palmar aponeurosis; it is absent in some people.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the palmaris longus
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor digitorum superficialis
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle, coronoid process, and anterior radius
muscles.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of digits two through five
muscles.actions: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints and assists wrist flexion.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the flexor digitorum superficialis
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor digitorum profundus
muscles.origin: Proximal anterior and medial ulna and adjacent interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of digits two through five
muscles.actions: Flexes the distal interphalangeal joints and assists flexion of the fingers and wrist.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the flexor digitorum profundus
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor pollicis longus
muscles.origin: Anterior radius and adjacent interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Flexes the thumb, particularly at the interphalangeal joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the flexor pollicis longus
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor carpi ulnaris
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus and posterior border of the ulna
muscles.insertion: Base of the fifth metacarpal
muscles.actions: Extends and adducts the hand at the wrist.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused posterior forearm illustration highlighting the extensor carpi ulnaris in purple
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor digitorum
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Extensor expansions of digits two through five
muscles.actions: Extends digits two through five and assists wrist extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the extensor digitorum
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Supinator
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle, radial collateral and annular ligaments, and supinator crest of the ulna
muscles.insertion: Proximal third of the radius
muscles.actions: Supinates the forearm, especially during unresisted or slow rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the supinator
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Pronator quadratus
muscles.origin: Distal anterior ulna
muscles.insertion: Distal anterior radius
muscles.actions: Pronates the forearm and helps stabilize the distal radioulnar joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the pronator quadratus
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Abductor pollicis brevis
muscles.origin: Flexor retinaculum and tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
muscles.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Abducts the thumb and assists opposition at the carpometacarpal joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting abductor pollicis brevis in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Opponens pollicis
muscles.origin: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of the trapezium
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the first metacarpal
muscles.actions: Opposes the thumb by drawing the first metacarpal across the palm with medial rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting opponens pollicis in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor pollicis
muscles.origin: Bases of the second and third metacarpals, capitate, and shaft of the third metacarpal
muscles.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Adducts the thumb toward the palm and contributes to pinch strength.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting adductor pollicis in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Lumbricals of the hand
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus
muscles.insertion: Lateral sides of the extensor expansions of digits two through five
muscles.actions: Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints while extending the interphalangeal joints of digits two through five.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting the hand lumbricals in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Dorsal interossei of the hand
muscles.origin: Adjacent sides of the metacarpals
muscles.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of digits two through four
muscles.actions: Abduct digits two through four from the middle-finger axis and assist coordinated finger flexion and extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting the dorsal interossei of the hand in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Vastus intermedius
muscles.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the femoral shaft
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity through the quadriceps tendon, patella, and patellar ligament
muscles.actions: Extends the leg at the knee as the deep central portion of the quadriceps femoris.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model highlighting the vastus intermedius beneath the superficial quadriceps
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor brevis
muscles.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
muscles.insertion: Pectineal line and proximal linea aspera of the femur
muscles.actions: Adducts the thigh and assists hip flexion and medial rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model highlighting the adductor brevis in the medial thigh
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Pectineus
muscles.origin: Pecten pubis and adjacent superior pubic ramus
muscles.insertion: Pectineal line of the femur
muscles.actions: Adducts and flexes the thigh and can assist medial rotation at the hip.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the pectineus in color at the proximal medial thigh
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Obturator internus
muscles.origin: Internal surface of the obturator membrane and surrounding pelvis
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter through the lesser sciatic foramen
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the extended thigh, abducts the flexed thigh, and stabilizes the femoral head.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior hip anatomy plate identifying the obturator internus
muscles.imageCredit: Mikael Häggström, after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Obturator externus
muscles.origin: External surface of the obturator membrane and margins of the obturator foramen
muscles.insertion: Trochanteric fossa of the femur
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the thigh and helps stabilize the femoral head in the acetabulum.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior hip anatomy plate with the obturator externus highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: Mikael Häggström, after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Superior gemellus
muscles.origin: Ischial spine
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter with the obturator internus tendon
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the extended thigh, abducts the flexed thigh, and stabilizes the hip joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior hip anatomy plate with the superior gemellus highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: Mikael Häggström, after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Inferior gemellus
muscles.origin: Upper part of the ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter with the obturator internus tendon
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates the extended thigh, abducts the flexed thigh, and stabilizes the hip joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior hip anatomy plate with the inferior gemellus highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: Mikael Häggström, after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Quadratus femoris
muscles.origin: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: Quadrate tubercle and adjacent intertrochanteric crest of the femur
muscles.actions: Laterally rotates and assists adduction of the thigh while stabilizing the hip joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior hip anatomy plate with the quadratus femoris highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: Mikael Häggström, after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Plantaris
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur and adjacent knee capsule
muscles.insertion: Posterior calcaneus, usually through a long thin tendon near the calcaneal tendon
muscles.actions: Weakly plantarflexes the ankle and flexes the knee; it is absent in some people.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy posterior leg plate highlighting the thin plantaris muscle and its long tendon
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter / Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Popliteus
muscles.origin: Lateral femoral condyle and lateral meniscus
muscles.insertion: Posterior tibia superior to the soleal line
muscles.actions: Unlocks the knee from full extension by medially rotating the tibia on the femur, and assists knee flexion and rotational control.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy posterior knee plate highlighting the popliteus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Vandyke Carter / Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Fibularis tertius
muscles.origin: Distal anterior fibula and adjacent interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Dorsal base of the fifth metatarsal
muscles.actions: Dorsiflexes and everts the foot; it may be absent in some people.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model distinctly highlighting the fibularis tertius muscle
muscles.imageCredit: DBCLS / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor digitorum brevis
muscles.origin: Superolateral surface of the calcaneus
muscles.insertion: Extensor tendons of toes two through four
muscles.actions: Assists extension of toes two through four.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model distinctly highlighting the extensor digitorum brevis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: DBCLS / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Abductor hallucis
muscles.origin: Medial calcaneal tubercle, flexor retinaculum, and plantar aponeurosis
muscles.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.actions: Abducts and flexes the great toe and supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the abductor hallucis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor digitorum brevis
muscles.origin: Medial calcaneal tubercle and plantar aponeurosis
muscles.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of toes two through five
muscles.actions: Flexes toes two through five at the proximal interphalangeal joints and supports the longitudinal arch.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the flexor digitorum brevis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Abductor digiti minimi of the foot
muscles.origin: Medial and lateral calcaneal tubercles and plantar aponeurosis
muscles.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe
muscles.actions: Abducts and flexes the fifth toe and contributes to lateral foot support.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the abductor digiti minimi of the foot
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Quadratus plantae
muscles.origin: Medial and lateral surfaces of the calcaneus
muscles.insertion: Posterolateral margin of the flexor digitorum longus tendon
muscles.actions: Assists flexor digitorum longus in flexing toes two through five and redirects its pull.
muscles.imageAlt: Plantar anatomical illustration highlighting the quadratus plantae muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Berichard after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Lumbricals of the foot
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus
muscles.insertion: Medial sides of the extensor expansions of toes two through five
muscles.actions: Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints while extending the interphalangeal joints of toes two through five.
muscles.imageAlt: Plantar Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the four lumbricals of the foot
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor hallucis brevis
muscles.origin: Plantar surfaces of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform
muscles.insertion: Both sides of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe through the sesamoids
muscles.actions: Flexes the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint and supports the medial forefoot.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the flexor hallucis brevis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Adductor hallucis
muscles.origin: Bases of metatarsals two through four and plantar ligaments of the lateral metatarsophalangeal joints
muscles.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.actions: Adducts the great toe, assists toe flexion, and supports the transverse arch.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the adductor hallucis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Plantar interossei of the foot
muscles.origin: Medial sides of metatarsals three through five
muscles.insertion: Medial bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of toes three through five
muscles.actions: Adduct toes three through five toward the second toe and assist coordinated toe flexion and extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused plantar anatomy plate distinctly highlighting the plantar interossei of the foot
muscles.imageCredit: Leo Testut, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Dorsal interossei of the foot
muscles.origin: Adjacent sides of the metatarsals
muscles.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of toes two through four
muscles.actions: Abduct toes two through four from the second-toe axis and assist coordinated toe flexion and extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused anatomical plate distinctly depicting the dorsal interossei of the foot
muscles.imageCredit: Leo Testut, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.title: Splenius cervicis
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Transverse processes of the upper cervical vertebrae
muscles.actions: Extends the neck bilaterally and rotates or laterally flexes it toward the working side.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior anatomical rendering highlighting the splenius cervicis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Longissimus cervicis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Transverse processes of the middle and upper cervical vertebrae
muscles.actions: Extends and laterally flexes the cervical vertebral column.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the longissimus column, including longissimus cervicis
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Semispinalis cervicis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Spinous processes of the cervical vertebrae
muscles.actions: Extends the cervical spine and rotates it toward the opposite side.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy plate highlighting the semispinalis family, including semispinalis cervicis
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Semispinalis thoracis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of the lower thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Spinous processes of upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae
muscles.actions: Extends the thoracic and cervical spine and assists contralateral rotation.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused posterior anatomy plate highlighting the semispinalis thoracis division of the semispinalis muscle column
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, modified by Uwe Gille, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Rotatores breves
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of vertebrae, most developed in the thoracic region
muscles.insertion: Lamina and spinous process of the vertebra immediately above
muscles.actions: Provide fine segmental stabilization and assist small extension and opposite-side rotation movements.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Anatomography rendering highlighting the rotatores breves short rotator series along the spine
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Rotatores longi
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of vertebrae, most developed in the thoracic region
muscles.insertion: Lamina and spinous process of the vertebra two levels above
muscles.actions: Support segmental proprioception and stability while assisting small extension and opposite-side rotation movements.
muscles.imageAlt: Posterior Anatomography rendering highlighting the rotatores longi long rotator series along the spine
muscles.imageCredit: BodyParts3D / Anatomography, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Interspinales cervicis
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of the lower cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Spinous process of the adjacent cervical vertebra above
muscles.actions: Assist local cervical extension and provide fine segmental stabilization.
muscles.imageAlt: English-labeled OpenStax deep-back anatomy plate providing regional reference for the cervical interspinales; the muscle is not individually highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax College, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Interspinales thoracis
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of thoracic vertebrae where these small muscles are present
muscles.insertion: Spinous process of the adjacent thoracic vertebra above
muscles.actions: Assist local thoracic extension and segmental control; they are less developed than in the cervical and lumbar regions.
muscles.imageAlt: English-labeled OpenStax deep-back anatomy plate providing regional reference for the thoracic interspinales; the muscle is not individually highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax College, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Interspinales lumborum
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of lumbar vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Spinous process of the adjacent lumbar vertebra above
muscles.actions: Assist local lumbar extension and provide fine segmental stabilization.
muscles.imageAlt: English-labeled OpenStax deep-back anatomy plate providing regional reference for the lumbar interspinales; the muscle is not individually highlighted
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax College, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Intertransversarii cervicis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of cervical vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Transverse process of the adjacent cervical vertebra
muscles.actions: Assist same-side cervical lateral flexion and provide fine segmental stabilization and proprioception.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy illustration identifying the intertransversarii cervicis between adjacent cervical transverse processes
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Intertransversarii lumborum
muscles.origin: Transverse and accessory processes of lumbar vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Transverse process of the adjacent lumbar vertebra
muscles.actions: Assist same-side lumbar lateral flexion and provide fine segmental stabilization and proprioception.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy illustration identifying the intertransversarii lumborum between adjacent lumbar transverse processes
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Head, Neck, and Back

muscles.title: Internal intercostals
muscles.origin: Inferior border of each rib and adjacent costal cartilage
muscles.insertion: Superior border of the rib below
muscles.actions: Draw the ribs together during forced expiration and stabilize the intercostal spaces.
muscles.imageAlt: Rotating Anatomography model highlighting the internal intercostals between adjacent ribs
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Innermost intercostals
muscles.origin: Inner surfaces of ribs near the costal groove
muscles.insertion: Inner surface of the adjacent rib below
muscles.actions: Assist the internal intercostals during forced expiration and stabilize adjacent ribs.
muscles.imageAlt: Inferior Anatomography rendering highlighting the innermost intercostals in red
muscles.imageCredit: Anatomography / DBCLS, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Levator ani
muscles.origin: Pubis, tendinous arch of obturator fascia, and ischial spine
muscles.insertion: Perineal body, walls of pelvic organs, anococcygeal ligament, and coccyx
muscles.actions: Supports pelvic viscera, elevates the pelvic floor, and contributes to continence.
muscles.imageAlt: Inferior pelvic illustration isolating and highlighting the female levator ani muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Uwe Gille after Gray's Anatomy, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Coccygeus (ischiococcygeus)
muscles.origin: Ischial spine and sacrospinous ligament
muscles.insertion: Lateral margins of the lower sacrum and coccyx
muscles.actions: Supports the pelvic viscera and draws the coccyx forward after defecation.
muscles.imageAlt: OpenStax pelvic floor diagram identifying the coccygeus ischiococcygeus muscle
muscles.imageCredit: OpenStax, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax

muscles.title: Coracobrachialis
muscles.origin: Coracoid process of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the medial humerus
muscles.actions: Flexes and adducts the arm at the shoulder and helps stabilize the humeral head.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the coracobrachialis muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Anconeus
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Lateral olecranon and proximal posterior ulna
muscles.actions: Assists elbow extension and stabilizes the elbow during forearm movement.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the anconeus muscle at the posterior elbow in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Base of the third metacarpal
muscles.actions: Extends and abducts the wrist and helps stabilize it during gripping.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Selket, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor digiti minimi
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Extensor expansion of the fifth digit
muscles.actions: Extends the little finger and assists wrist extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor digiti minimi muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Abductor pollicis longus
muscles.origin: Posterior ulna, radius, and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the first metacarpal
muscles.actions: Abducts and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the abductor pollicis longus muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor pollicis brevis
muscles.origin: Posterior radius and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint and assists wrist abduction.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor pollicis brevis muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor pollicis longus
muscles.origin: Posterior ulna and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Extends the thumb at the interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor pollicis longus muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Extensor indicis
muscles.origin: Posterior distal ulna and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Extensor expansion of the index finger
muscles.actions: Extends the index finger independently and assists wrist extension.
muscles.imageAlt: Gray's Anatomy illustration highlighting the extensor indicis muscle in red
muscles.imageCredit: Gray's Anatomy, highlighted by Helgo13, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
muscles.sourceName: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

muscles.title: Flexor pollicis brevis
muscles.origin: Flexor retinaculum and adjacent carpal bones
muscles.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
muscles.actions: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint and assists opposition.
muscles.imageAlt: Focused Gray anatomy plate highlighting flexor pollicis brevis in red
muscles.imageCredit: Henry Gray, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
